# Clerk Auth for mapstack-us — Research Findings (Aug 2026)

## Clerk Free Tier Facts
Clerk's Hobby plan currently offers **50,000 MRU** (Monthly *Retained* Users, not MAU) free per app — a user only counts once they return at least one day after signup, making MRU narrower/harder-to-trigger than the MAU metric competitors use ([clerk.com/pricing](https://clerk.com/pricing)). This replaced the long-standing 10,000-free-user tier on **Feb 5, 2026** ([clerk.com/blog/new-pricing-plans](https://clerk.com/blog/new-pricing-plans), [saasprices.net](https://saasprices.net/blog/clerk-free-plan-changes)) — the second time Clerk has materially reshaped its pricing model, so further changes should be assumed possible. Free tier excludes MFA, passkeys, custom email templates, SAML/OIDC enterprise connections, SMS codes, bans/allowlists, and simultaneous sessions; includes basic auth, unlimited apps, custom domain, webhooks, 7-day sessions, 1-day log retention. **Exceeding the cap does not hard-block immediately** — Clerk requires upgrading to Pro with a one-month grace period. **Pro is $25/mo** (includes 50k MRU, ~$0.02/MRU/mo overage with volume discounts); **Business is $300/mo** (SOC 2 report access, 30-day logs). At 1,000–10,000 MAU, a project like mapstack-us would sit entirely inside the free tier under current terms ([clerk.com/pricing](https://clerk.com/pricing)).

## Open Source / Lock-in Verdict
Clerk is **not open source**. Its frontend/backend SDKs are published on GitHub, but they are auto-generated wrappers around Clerk's proprietary, closed Backend API and hosted dashboard — the actual auth engine and session store are SaaS-only ([clerk.com/docs SDK dev guide](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/development/sdk-development/backend-only)). Migration risk is moderate: Clerk lets you export users and password hashes via CSV/API and has an official migration tool ([github.com/clerk/migration-tool](https://github.com/clerk/migration-tool)), and third-party guides exist for migrating to WorkOS or Better Auth. The real lock-in is architectural (session model, middleware, auth calls baked into the app) rather than data-export ([LeanVibe analysis](https://leanvibe.io/blog/bp-08831)).

## Clerk Security Posture
SOC 2 Type II certified since **May 6, 2022** (report gated to Business plan+) ([clerk.com/articles/clerk-security-how-we-protect-your-users](https://clerk.com/articles/clerk-security-how-we-protect-your-users)). GDPR-compliant via EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework plus UK/Swiss extensions; also covers CCPA/LGPD/APPI. **No data-residency options** — all data on US infrastructure (GCP + Cloudflare). Sessions use 60-second JWTs refreshed every 50s via split HttpOnly/JS-exposed cookies. Track record: 5 CVEs disclosed Jan 2024–Apr 2026, patched within days — most notably **CVE-2024-22206**, a critical (CVSS 9.4) auth-bypass in `@clerk/nextjs` affecting versions since Jan 2023, no known exploitation ([Snyk advisory](https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-CLERKNEXTJS-6156632)). Reliability has been rocky recently: a **Feb 19, 2026 outage** took sign-in/account management down for ~90 minutes (95%+ requests returning 429) due to a Postgres query-plan flip, one of six published postmortems between Feb 2025–Mar 2026 ([clerk.com postmortem](https://clerk.com/blog/2026-02-19-system-outage-postmortem)).

## Alternatives Comparison

| Option | Status/Cost | Maturity | Key Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Auth.js/NextAuth** | Fully OSS, self-hosted, $0 forever, no MAU billing | Mature but now maintenance-mode only ([Better Auth absorbed the team, Sept 2025](https://dev.to/pipipi-dev/nextauthjs-to-better-auth-why-i-switched-auth-libraries-31h3)) | Not recommended for new projects; you own patching/migrations |
| **Better-Auth** | OSS (MIT core, free forever), enterprise add-ons paid | Production-ready, 28,600+ GitHub stars, 150k+ weekly downloads, YC-backed, absorbed Auth.js in 2026 ([github.com/better-auth/better-auth](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth)) | Younger than Clerk/Auth0 at massive scale; SSO/SCIM are paid |
| **Supabase Auth** | Free: 50,000 real MAU, bundled with DB/storage | Mature, widely used | Still a hosted SaaS with its own future pricing risk, just consolidated with DB vendor ([uibakery.io](https://uibakery.io/blog/supabase-pricing)) |
| **Lucia** | Deprecated ~March 2025 by maintainer; only security patches under Better Auth umbrella now | **Dead as a library** — repositioned as a learn-to-build-your-own reference, not installable ([wisp.blog](https://www.wisp.blog/blog/lucia-auth-is-dead-whats-next-for-auth), [GitHub discussion](https://github.com/lucia-auth/lucia/discussions/1714)) | Do not recommend for new use |

## Recommendation
Clerk's 50k-MRU free tier is quota-safe for a niche hobby dataviz app for years — the real exposure is pricing-model volatility (already changed once) and SaaS dependency (a 90-min outage in Feb 2026, no data residency), not hitting the cap. Given mapstack-us's OSS/$0 ethos, **Better-Auth** is the better long-term bet: actively developed, MIT-licensed, production-ready, and eliminates vendor-billing risk permanently, at the cost of modest self-maintenance (patches, session code) that's manageable for a low-traffic solo project. Avoid Lucia (dead) and new Auth.js adoption (maintenance-mode). If a database gets added anyway, Supabase Auth is a reasonable single-vendor alternative to Better-Auth+external DB.
